context: Prefer one DuckDB-WASM query that joins existing result_environment and query_executions. Do not bump the read-model version or edit explorer_pipeline unless those tables are absent from the live snapshot.
description:
Two blocked pieces of explorer-basis-browse-hardware-engine-facets share one root cause: the read model's cohort index tables carry neither hardware identity nor per-execution data, so the index pages cannot show either.

VERIFIED against a read-model-v8 snapshot:
  - benchmark_rankings carries no hardware column at all
  - platform_index_rows carries only driver_version / platform_version
  - arch, cpu_family and cpu_model live in result_environment and result_detail_metrics, which are per-result detail tables neither index page queries
  - the only executions accessor is getQueryExecutions(resultId), one result per call

BLOCKED PIECE 1 (deferral #723) - architecture and CPU columns on BenchmarkIndex and PlatformIndex.

BLOCKED PIECE 2 (deferral #724) - the median-or-min basis control on the index pages. NOT blocked by data volume: the largest cohort is 12 runs / 972 execution rows, whole corpus 22136 rows, native DuckDB fetch 3 ms, against interaction budgets of 500 ms p50 / 1000 ms p95. It is blocked by query SHAPE - a non-default basis for a cohort is N queries where N is the run count, growing with the corpus.

Both fixes live outside that item's allowlist: adding columns means _project/scripts/explorer_pipeline/ (plus a read-model version bump), and a bulk executions accessor means results-explorer/src/lib/duckdbQueries.ts.

Neither was worked around client-side on purpose. Looping the per-result accessor is exactly the N-query shape the performance budget is at risk from.

anti_patterns.instead: issue one bulk query for the cohort
anti_patterns.why: the original block was the N-query shape, not missing client joins

anti_patterns.dont: rewrite explorer_pipeline or bump the read-model version first
anti_patterns.instead: join result_environment and query_executions already in the snapshot

Index pages must not issue one getQueryExecutions() call per row.

Extend getQueryExecutions with a bulk cohort accessor rather than adding a second per-result API.

work_units.evidence:
Probed the live read-model-v10 snapshot (results-explorer/public/data/results.duckdb, copied read-only) with native duckdb 1.4.4.

Tables present and sufficient: result_environment (244 rows, arch non-null 201, cpu_family 199, cpu_model 199), query_executions (41812 rows), result_basis_availability (244 rows = full coverage of all 244 benchmark_rankings rows).

PROOF 1 - hardware attaches in one query: benchmark_rankings LEFT JOIN result_environment USING (result_id) for the tpch/sf0.01/power cohort returns 15/15 rows in 8 ms (12 with arch, 15 with cpu_model). Whole ranking table joined in 1 ms: 166 ranking-eligible rows, 164 arch, 130 cpu_family/cpu_model. No pipeline change or read-model bump needed.

PROOF 2 - cohort executions in one query: SELECT ... FROM query_executions WHERE result_id IN (cohort subquery) returns 1236 rows / 15 runs for the largest cohort (tpch sf0.01 power) in 2 ms. Across all cohorts exec volume is min 192 / median 440 / max 4536 rows; whole-corpus count 41812 in <1 ms native. That is one query, not N, and far inside the 500 ms p50 / 1000 ms p95 interaction budget.

PROOF 3 - a non-default basis is a real choice here, not a collapsed one: run_type/status vocabulary is measurement|pass 31085, warmup|pass 10362, measurement|fail 274, warmup|fail 91; every result records exactly 3 passing measurement passes (min 3 / median 3 / max 3 distinct iters), so min and median reduce genuinely different samples.

PROOF 4 - hardware columns are informative rather than constant: 2 distinct arch (x86_64, arm64), 3 cpu_family (apple_silicon, amd_epyc, intel_xeon), 5 cpu_model; 6 cohorts contain more than one distinct arch and the same 6 contain more than one cpu_family, so a per-row hardware column carries real signal.
